subject: Veridian: request for SDLC change-control + secrets handoff artifacts
messages:
From: Claire DuPont <claire.dupont@veridian.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: security-assessor@veridian.com
Date: 2028-02-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: SDLC artifact ask: change approvals + secrets handoff snapshot

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for taking this intake. For Veridian's SIG/SOC2 review we need a focused package on your change control and secrets management practices tied to releases. Can you provide the following by EOD Thu 2028-02-17: 

1) A chronological export of change approvals for all production merges in Q4 2027 (PR IDs, approver, timestamp, brief reason if exception).
2) CI job logs or summaries showing ephemeral credential issuance and teardown for the same merges (redacted where necessary).
3) A ledger or matrix describing how short-lived secrets are handed between CI agents and deploy runners, including who has stewarding responsibility.
4) Any documented deviations/branch protection exceptions and approver records for those deviations.
5) If you have a short-run walkthrough/demo (15–20m) of the pre-deploy gating and secret handback flow, that would be ideal.

Two quick clarifying Qs: do you accept SHA256 checksums instead of raw private keys for artifact verification? And do you prefer we receive artifacts via a shared Drive folder or an encrypted bundle through our secure upload portal?

Appreciate the help — Veridian is aiming to close this control area on Friday.

Best,
Claire DuPont
Principal Security Assessor
Veridian Risk & Assurance

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Claire DuPont <claire.dupont@veridian.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-02-14T09:48:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SDLC artifact ask: change approvals + secrets handoff snapshot

Claire — thanks for the clear list. We're on it and can meet the timeline. Quick plan:

- I'll own the intake and delivery (soojin).
- Irene will assemble the chronological change-approval export and branch exception matrix.
- Jordan will collect CI job step attestations and produce redacted logs for ephemeral-secret issuance/teardown.
- Marissa will validate the stewarding matrix and provide the owner contact info for each stewarded secret group.

On your two questions: we can provide SHA256 checksums in lieu of raw private material for artifact integrity verification. For transfer, Drive folder with enforced viewer restrictions is preferable (we will also publish an encrypted archive if you require it).

I'll start a shared Drive folder and attach a preliminary manifest with what we intend to deliver. If you can confirm that checksums are acceptable, we'll avoid including any private key material. Also indicate if you want console-recorded demo or a live Zoom walkthrough.

Deliverables we expect to drop into the Drive by Thu EOD (UTC):
- change-control-chronicle-2027Q4.csv (PR id, commit, approver, timestamp, exception flag)
- ci-step-attestation-redacted.log (CI steps that mint ephemeral creds + teardown)
- ephemeral-secret-handoff-ledger.xlsx (mapping stewards and TTLs)
- branch-exception-matrix.pdf (summary of branch-protection bypasses with approvals)

I'll include a JIRA link in the folder for cross-reference (JIRA-7291).

Thanks — talk soon.

Soojin Lee
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Claire DuPont <claire.dupont@veridian.com>
Date: 2028-02-15T11:06:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SDLC artifact ask: change approvals + secrets handoff snapshot

Team / Claire — attaching the artifacts we committed to in the plan. Notes inline: 

Attachments (stubs):
- change-control-chronicle-2027Q4.csv (CSV export from our PR gating system. Columns: pr_id, commit_sha, author, approver, approval_time_utc, exception_flag, exception_reason). Sensitive fields redacted where relevant.
- ci-step-attestation-redacted.log (a concatenated view of the CI pipeline runs for the listed PRs. Keys and tokens redacted; we include hashed token IDs and lifecycle timestamps).
- ephemeral-secret-handoff-ledger.xlsx (mapping rows: secret_group, issuing_job, TTL_seconds, steward, last_rotation_iso).
- branch-exception-matrix.pdf (PDF that aggregates every branch policy override and the approver audit note).

Implementation notes: our CI uses ephemeral short-lived credentials (20–90s lifetimes for runner-level tokens) minted by the build agent. The log shows the mint event (hashed_id), issuance_time, consumer_id, and teardown event. Teardown is automatic via the runner supervisor — you can see the teardown timestamps correlated to the mint events.

Drive link (internal): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cSDLC-EVIDENCE — I set viewer + comment restrictions and added Claire's account.

JIRA: JIRA-7291 contains the crosswalk between PR IDs and the artifacts above.

If Veridian wants to validate a specific commit in a live session, I can run a short demo to reproduce the mint/teardown lifecycle from our staging runner.

-Jordan
Senior CI Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Claire DuPont <claire.dupont@veridian.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-02-16T08:34:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SDLC artifact ask: change approvals + secrets handoff snapshot

Thanks Jordan — the deliverables look good at a glance. A couple of follow-ups after a quick pass: 

1) In the CSV I can see two PRs where the approver field is empty (PR #1742 and PR #1819). Can you confirm whether those were auto-merged by a bot or if the approval record was recorded in another system (and point us to that record)?
2) In the ephemeral-secret-handoff-ledger.xlsx the steward column lists a team alias for two secret groups ("infra-ci-runners") rather than an owner name. For SOC2 traceability we need a named steward and an on-call contact (email). Can Marissa provide those?
3) For the ci-step-attestation-redacted.log you provided hashed token IDs — please also include the SHA256 checksum of the unredacted job artifact tarball so we can verify the mapping without requesting private tokens.

We'd prefer to do a 20-minute live walkthrough on Friday 2028-02-18 at 10:00 PT. If that works for your team, we'll send a calendar invite.

Claire

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Claire DuPont <claire.dupont@veridian.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-02-18T15:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SDLC artifact ask: change approvals + secrets handoff snapshot

Claire — quick status update ahead of the walkthrough: 

- PR #1742 and PR #1819 were auto-merged by the release bot after an external security scan completed; the approval was recorded in the release-bot audit log (column release_audit_id in the CSV). I added an additional column 'approval_source' and attached an updated CSV in the Drive.
- Marissa: please add named stewards and on-call emails for any rows that have a team alias in ephemeral-secret-handoff-ledger.xlsx.
- Jordan: please append SHA256 checksums for the job artifact tarballs to ci-step-attestation-redacted.log and drop the updated file in the Drive.

We confirm Friday 2028-02-18 10:00 PT for the 20-minute walkthrough — I'll accept the calendar invite once Claire sends. We'll plan a live demo of token mint -> runner consumption -> teardown using a staging run so no production keys are shown.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cSDLC-EVIDENCE (updated artifacts uploaded).

Soojin Lee
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference
